statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission) Online Filing System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet; any of the 11 official South African languages may be used, but transliteration into English characters is required for names not already in Roman script; names must end with the legal suffix '(Pty) Ltd' or 'Proprietary Limited'; only alphanumeric characters, spaces, and limited punctuation are permitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a name reservation, the applicant may file a written representation via the CIPC Online Filing System within 30 days of rejection. If the objection is sustained, the applicant may submit a formal administrative appeal to the Companies Tribunal under Section 31 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 within 30 days of the CIPC's decision. Legal representation is recommended but not mandatory for the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for this digital health app industry provided it renders a physical street address in South Africa for official service of process and maintains a dedicated document-receiving service; a P.O. Box or non-physical address is not acceptable. A serviced or virtual office with a registered street address and access during normal business hours is generally accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 5–15% per annum) for non-hazardous digital technology service providers; no mandatory unannounced CIPC inspections, but SARS and Department of Labour retain inspection powers to verify commercial substance and registered office accessibility.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended; s 13 (incorporation), s 14 (notice of incorporation), s 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), s 19 (effect of incorporation), s 66 (board of directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (the dtic)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital or escrow requirement under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; a Proprietary Limited (Pty) Ltd may be incorporated with zero issued shares, although at least one share is recommended for practical purposes; any stated capital must be fully paid in cash or kind before allotment if required by the Memorandum of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The subscribers named in the Memorandum of Incorporation be and are hereby allotted the initial ordinary shares of the Company at par value, and the Directors are authorised to issue share certificates accordingly. 2. The registered office of the Company be and is hereby adopted as the address stated in the Notice of Incorporation, and the Company is authorised to commence business from that address. 3. The following persons be and are hereby appointed as Directors and office-bearers: [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Company Secretary, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting. 4. The Directors are authorised to file all necessary statutory forms with CIPC and SARS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Pre-incorporation Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an availability search on CIPC's name database, then file a CoR 9.2 name reservation application online. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 6 months. Proceed to prepare incorporation documents once reservation is granted.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged as undesirable or confusingly similar, file an objection or apply for a new name; administrative review may be requested under Companies Act s 160 within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Memorandum of Incorporation and Board Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel / Company Secretary (pre-filing internal step)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) in accordance with Companies Act s 15, covering shares, director authority, quorum, and any restrictive conditions. Prepare minutes of the first board meeting, a register of directors, and a share register.
required_dossiers: Notice of registered office and postal address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Not a filing step; ensure the MOI does not contravene the Companies Act to avoid subsequent rejection by CIPC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgement of Notice of Incorporation with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete CoR 14.1 and upload executed MOI (CoR 15.1), consent forms, and proof of name reservation. Pay the government filing fee by credit card or electronic funds transfer. Submit electronically; CIPC will issue a CoR 14.2 registration certificate upon approval.
required_dossiers: Copy of identity documents of directors and incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a query or rejection, correct the flagged fields within the prescribed response period (usually 10 business days) and resubmit; escalation to CIPC's client support office or the Companies Tribunal may be used for procedural issues.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS Tax Registration and Beneficial Ownership Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) and CIPC Beneficial Ownership Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for an income tax reference number via SARS eFiling, register for Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) if hiring employees, apply for VAT if annual turnover is expected to exceed R1 million, and file beneficial ownership information with CIPC within 30 days of incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS rejects or queries the application, provide additional documentation through eFiling; for the Beneficial Ownership Register, update CIPC's online portal promptly to maintain good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Department of Employment and Labour Registration (UIF and COIDA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) contributions and obtain a COIDA claim number for occupational injuries if the company will have employees. This step is not mandatory for a purely digital single-owner company but is advisable for any payroll or workplace activity.
required_dossiers: Approval from local municipality if physical office is leased
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is queried, verify that the business classification (ISIC 6201) is correctly reflected and resubmit with additional employee affidavits or a letter from the accounting officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Adoption and Physical Address Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC (registered office); municipality for zoning compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the registered office address at the first board meeting and file any change with CIPC. Obtain a lease agreement or letter of availability from the premises owner, and confirm municipal zoning permits for the physical location.
required_dossiers: Municipal zoning certificate (if physical office); home-office exemption documents for digital-only operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office address is rejected, provide an alternative South African address and file a CoR 14.1 amendment to CIPC.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the undertaking is a digital services provider classified under ISIC 6201 (Computer programming) and does not require an industrial manufacturing license from the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition or any municipal industrial authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no operating or manufacturing permit required for a software/health-app business in South Africa.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is a purely digital service with no physical manufacturing, no effluent discharge, and no atmospheric emissions; no EIA registration or report required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A – zero industrial discharge; all electronic equipment must comply with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008, Part 8 (E-waste disposal), and POPIA data protection standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and occupational health and safety clearance required only if the company leases a physical office; otherwise, the home-office workplace must comply with the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 general duty clauses and municipal zoning regulations for a home enterprise.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); official portal: www.sars.gov.za and SARS eFiling
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign (non-resident) entity carrying on an enterprise in South Africa, or supplying electronic services to South African customers, must obtain an income tax reference number by submitting the non-resident taxpayer registration application via SARS eFiling or at a SARS branch, accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, memorandum of incorporation, English-translated constitutional documents, proof of director/beneficial-owner identity, and a signed power of attorney appointing a SARS-recognised local representative where required. After income tax registration, the entity applies for VAT vendor registration through the VAT 101 application (or the dedicated Foreign Supplier of Electronic Services registration), submitting the foreign tax status certificate, banking confirmation, and e-commerce platform agreements; SARS issues a VAT registration number upon verification, after which VAT 201 returns must be filed electronically and payments made through eFiling on a monthly or bi-monthly cycle. Failure to complete SARS beneficial-ownership and risk verification may result in delayed registration or refusal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a (Pty) Ltd incorporated or effectively managed in South Africa is a tax resident taxed on worldwide income at the 27% corporate income tax rate. Non-resident shareholders receive no pass-through treatment and are separately subject to dividends tax on distributions. Territorial sourcing rules apply only to non-resident taxpayers without South African effective management, and no general tax-exempt zone applies to the technology sector.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a US-style check-the-box classification regime; a private company is mandatorily taxed as an entity. Relevant elections and statutory mechanisms for a digital health app group include: (i) Small Business Corporation status under section 12E (progressive corporate tax rates for qualifying closely-held companies); (ii) Headquarter Company election under section 9I, subject to 80% foreign-shareholding and activity composition tests and prior SARS approval; (iii) functional currency election under section 25D; (iv) CFC high-tax exemption election under section 9D(9) for foreign subsidiaries subject to tax at no less than 70% of the South African normal tax; and (v) mandatory, non-elective hybrid mismatch adjustments under sections 8I and 8J of the Income Tax Act No. 58 of 1962, which disallow deductions in respect of hybrid financial instruments and hybrid entity arrangements producing double-dip outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act No. 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory vendor registration applies when taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any rolling 12-month period for resident suppliers; voluntary registration is available from ZAR 50,000. Foreign suppliers of electronic services (e.g., subscription and in-app purchase revenue from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing to South African customers) are compulsorily registrable when their taxable supplies of electronic services to South African recipients exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period, with no requirement of a local physical presence or fixed establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC) gateway, or tax-authority digital stamping is currently in force. SARS operates a voluntary e-invoicing pilot aligned with the PEPPOL/UBL standard and requires: (i) full tax invoices under section 20(4) of the VAT Act, or simplified invoices for supplies below ZAR 5,000; (ii) electronic filing and payment of VAT 201 returns via eFiling on the assigned monthly or bi-monthly cycle; (iii) real-time data matching of eFiling declarations, bank account data, and third-party payment-provider reporting received from Apple and Google; and (iv) retention of electronic records for at least five years under section 55 of the Tax Administration Act No. 28 of 2011. Foreign e-services suppliers must issue documents carrying their SARS vendor number and statutory content, and are subject to SARS data-analytics-driven verification rather than per-invoice pre-approval.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under section 11(1) of the VAT Act where the goods are supplied to a non-resident and removed from South Africa within 90 days of the date of supply. Services are zero-rated under section 11(2)(l) where supplied to a non-resident who is outside South Africa at the time of supply, provided the services do not relate to land or movable property situated in South Africa, are not physically rendered in South Africa, and do not constitute intellectual property exploited in South Africa. For the Health Fitness App Tracker, subscription fees and biometric telemetry services sold to non-resident end users through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing may qualify for zero-rating only where the substantive conditions of section 11(2)(l) are demonstrably satisfied; B2C app-store sales to South African users are standard-rated at 15%, and development or data-processing services rendered to non-residents outside South Africa may be zero-rated if the required documentary evidence is maintained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500 / electronic customs release) for goods
Commercial invoice and VAT zero-rating certificate
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank confirmation of receipt of export proceeds from the authorised dealer
Proof of non-resident status of the recipient (service contracts, identification, or corporate registration evidence)
Apple/Google payment-provider settlement reports and app-store analytics supporting jurisdictional allocation of each transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS subjects export zero-rating to intensive verification using customs export data, forex surveillance, and third-party data. Unsubstantiated or fraudulent zero-rating triggers: (i) additional assessments and clawback of output VAT with prescription extended to five years on material non-disclosure and unlimited in cases of fraud; (ii) interest at the prescribed rate under the Prescribed Rate of Interest Act; (iii) understatement penalties under sections 222-223 of the Tax Administration Act ranging from 10% (standard case) to 150% (intentional tax evasion or gross negligence); (iv) additional tax under section 60 of the VAT Act for failure to account or false statements; (v) administrative non-compliance penalties up to ZAR 16,000 per month; and (vi) criminal prosecution with fines and imprisonment for deliberate evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), acting under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961 (Government Notice R1111).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is a partially convertible currency. Current-account transactions (goods, services, dividends, royalties, app-store settlement receipts) are processed by authorised dealers without SARB pre-approval, subject to documentary verification and balance-of-payments (BI) reporting. Capital-account transactions (non-resident equity subscription, external borrowings, offshore investments) require authorised-dealer consent or FinSurv approval on prescribed forms (Form A for share issues; Form C for external loans). ZAR is not fully outward-transferable; non-resident capital remittances are permitted only against the documented inward listing of funds. Profit repatriation is permitted on proof of tax clearance (SARS), signed financial statements, and dividend declaration, with withholding taxes applied at source.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Digital-service export proceeds (including Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlements) are treated as current-account receipts under the Exchange Control Regulations. Exporters must receive payment within 180 days of the invoice/export date and must surrender the foreign currency to an authorised dealer in exchange for rand within 30 days of receipt, unless FinSurv approval is granted for an approved foreign-currency account. The standard practice for a ZA (Pty) Ltd digital app publisher is automatic conversion of USD/EUR settlement proceeds to ZAR on the day of credit, with the authorised dealer capturing the BI declaration under service code 274 (computer and information services).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.mandatory_conversion_ratio: 100% of export/app-sale proceeds must be converted to ZAR via an authorised dealer unless a specific exemption or approved foreign-currency account is obtained; no partial conversion ratio is elective for a standard operational account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: ZAR Operational Current Account with inward-listed non-resident capital sub-account
Business Transactional Account (ZAR) with USD settlement feeder for app-store receipts
Corporate Current Account (ZAR) and SWIFT-enabled foreign-currency settlement account (USD/GBP/EUR)
Business Current Account (ZAR) with integrated trade-finance and FEC desk
Corporate Private Banking Current Account (ZAR) with discretionary FX facility for high-value treasury

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low as a primary ZAR treasury and settlement account; Medium as a supplementary offshore USD/EUR payout rail. South Africa does not operate an EMI licensing regime equivalent to the UK or EU; non-bank fintechs function only as 'authorised dealers with limited authority' or through a commercial-bank sponsor under SARB FinSurv supervision. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex) cannot obtain direct access to the ZAR real-time clearing system (SAMOS/RTCS) and cannot provide ZAR business accounts without a local banking partnership. They remain viable only for minor cross-border contractor payouts in GBP/EUR/USD, while all Apple/Google settlement receipts must be directed to a registered South African bank account for export-proceeds surrender compliance and BI filing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FICA (Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001) imposes full corporate customer due diligence: CIPC registration certificate, Memorandum of Incorporation, beneficial-ownership register with percentage thresholds, board resolution appointing signatories, and verified identity and address for each signatory and ultimate beneficial owner. In practice, Tier 1 banks mandate in-branch biometric verification of at least one director/signatory who is a South African resident; fully remote onboarding of an entirely non-resident board is not granted except under enhanced due diligence with apostilled passports and notarised attestations. Recommended structure: appoint a ZA-resident director or authorised signatory to perform the physical KYC interview, supported by certified documentation from non-resident shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs and directors without local presence, creating PEP and source-of-funds uncertainty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC extract and MOI; FICA-compliant UBO declaration (Form FIC-02 style) with proof of identity and address; apostilled certified passports; source-of-wealth statement (bank statements, investment history); board resolution; SARS tax clearance status pin for entity and controlling persons; written AML statement confirming no cash-intensive or crypto-linked inflows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-value inbound credits from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing flagged as potential layering or unauthorised money transmission.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Distribution Agreement; publisher/merchant IDs; monthly settlement statements in ZAR/USD; app-store analytics dashboard (downloads, revenue by geo); written explanation of merchant-of-record model confirming the company never holds end-customer funds; first three months of reconsolated transaction history; refund and chargeback policy documentation; POPIA compliance register for health/fitness data handling.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound USD/EUR payments to cloud, telemetry, and marketing vendors without a recognised services contract.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed cloud service agreements (AWS, Google Cloud) and detailed vendor invoices; service-level descriptions and data-flow architecture; annual USD expenditure forecast; transfer-pricing policy memo for any intercompany or management-fee flows; SARS good-standing certificate; authorised-dealer mandate letter confirming underlying commercial reason.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible-asset concentration (source code, health data, proprietary algorithms) raising IP ownership and royalty-flow questions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deed of cession/IP assignment evidencing company ownership; licences with Apple/Google as distributors; registered design/trademark extracts where applicable; confirmation that no unapproved royalty agreements currently remit to non-residents; if royalties are paid, draft royalty agreement submitted to SARB FinSurv with evidence of 15% (or DTA-reduced) withholding tax remittance and SARS receipt.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders transfer USD/EUR via SWIFT MT103 to the company's inward-listed capital account held with an authorised dealer, using the inward-equity purpose code (BOP Direct Investment: Equity, code 3610) and clear narrative 'Share subscription - inward direct investment'. The company files Form A (Application for approval of share issue to non-residents) with CIPC allotment records; the authorised dealer converts funds to ZAR on the same value date and maintains the inward listing record for future dividend/interest remittances. No SARB pre-approval is required for an ordinary share subscription in a private company provided the business does not fall within a restricted sector and no 'loop structure' (non-resident re-borrowing) is triggered. Funds are released to the operational account only after the inward declaration is captured.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Local operating disbursements clear through the South African Multiple Option Settlement (SAMOS) real-time gross settlement system via the bank's online channel. Cross-border disbursements (cloud hosting, software subscriptions, foreign contractors, licensing fees) are effected via SWIFT MT103 using applicable BOP service codes (274 for computer/information services; 279 for royalties/licences) with supporting invoices and service agreements retained on file. Commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT710) are not required for digital-service trade and are reserved for physical hardware/device procurement; where used, an irrevocable confirmed at-sight LC is the default rail. Apple/Google settlement receipts are matched to BI filings and any excess foreign currency is immediately surrendered; dividend, interest, and royalty remittances are executed as current-account payments through the authorised dealer subject to SARS tax clearance and the prescribed declaration forms.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward exchange contracts (FECs) - deliverable ZAR/USD (and ZAR/EUR) forwards concluded with a local authorised dealer against committed operational liabilities or identified receivable streams, supported by annual treasury policy documentation.
European-style OTC FX options - premium-purchased put and call options for USD outflows via the authorised dealer; option writing is not permitted without FinSurv approval.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (ZAR/USD) - permitted for hedging long-term external debt or intercompany funding obtained under Form C approval; FinSurv notification required.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) - offshore branch NDFs permissible as back-to-back overlays on deliverable FECs where physical ZAR settlement is impractical; such NDFs must be concluded through the authorised dealer and supported by an underlying commercial exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of approximately ZAR 180 (approx USD 10) per month or part of a month; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers CIPC deregistration procedure under s.82 of the Companies Act (administrative strike-off).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) and independent audit/review report, where required by Companies Act 2008, ss.84–90
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (filing required only for public, state-owned, or specifically directed companies); otherwise AFS must be prepared and presented to directors/shareholders and retained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS must be prepared within 6 months after financial year-end; audit/review report must be issued before director approval; CIPC filing, if applicable, is required in conjunction with the annual return cycle or as directed by CIPC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare and present AFS is a breach of the Companies Act; CIPC may issue a compliance notice, impose a fine, or seek administrative penalty if a filing obligation is mandated.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Register annual confirmation and filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneous with annual return filing; any change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the Register of Beneficial Ownership and filed with CIPC within 30 calendar days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with s.56B is an offence; late or inaccurate filings may result in CIPC administrative penalties, compliance notices, and potential restriction of the company's good standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is compulsory where the public-interest score (PIS) equals or exceeds 350 in the relevant financial year (Regulation 26(2)); if PIS is 100–349, a private company must have its AFS independently reviewed unless an audit is required by the MOI, shareholders, or CIPC. No audit or review is statutorily mandated if PIS is below 100 and no other trigger exists.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB for public companies and companies in the public interest; IFRS for SMEs, as adopted in South Africa, for qualifying private companies. Financial statements must include statement of financial position, statement of profit or loss and other comprehensive income, statement of changes in equity, and statement of cash flows (s.29 Companies Act).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual return must include confirmation of beneficial ownership details. The company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register and file a current copy with CIPC each year. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be reflected in the Register of Members and the Beneficial Ownership Register within 30 calendar days, with the updated BO register filed with CIPC within the same period.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Section 11D R&D tax incentive: 150% deduction for qualifying R&D expenditure; SEZ regime: 15% corporate rate for qualifying activities in industrial development zones; Small Business Corporation (SBC) graduated rates: 0% up to ZAR 100,000, 7% for ZAR 100,001–ZAR 250,000, 21% for ZAR 250,001–ZAR 500,000, 27% above ZAR 500,000 (subject to gross income threshold below ZAR 20 million).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 Corporate Income Tax Return, filed electronically via SARS eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 12 months from the end of the company's financial year (year of assessment), unless an extension is granted by SARS; provisional tax returns (IRP6) are due at the end of the 6th month of the year, at year-end, and optionally 6 months after year-end for taxpayers whose taxable income exceeds the applicable threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Turnover (domestic and export sales, net of VAT and trade discounts)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a permanent establishment (PE) in South Africa must report gross receipts attributable to the PE; app subscription revenue from South African users must be included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income (turnover plus sundry income, royalties, interest, and deemed capital gains)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all amounts accrued, excluding exempt income; digital payments from Apple IAP/Google Play are taxable to the extent they relate to South African users.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income (e.g., local tax-exempt dividends, foreign dividend exemptions, Section 12B energy incentives realised)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: South Africa-source dividends are exempt; foreign dividends may be exempt under participation exemption if holding >=10%. Complete the applicable boxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and allowances (operating expenses under s11, capital allowances under s12, and R&D deductions under s11D)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may deduct expenses directly attributable to South African PE income; app development and cloud costs must be apportioned on an arm's length basis.
Compute the PE's attributable profit; use the final BAT (balance of business) assessment to allocate global app income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss brought forward (must satisfy s20A continuity-of-trade test)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned Pty Ltd that underwent a shareholding change during the year must prove the same trade to sustain loss carryforward; otherwise the loss lapses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable before rebates (taxable income multiplied by 27%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the statutory rate; if an SBC, apply graduated tables; for SEZ income, apply 15% if a tax status certificate is held.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax payments made (IRP6 returns and amounts settled)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: First payment due within six months of year-start; second at year-end; third at six months post-year-end for taxable income above threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding taxes, rebates, and prepayments (foreign tax credits, dividends tax credits, PAYE for staff)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits under s6quat if treaty/double-tax agreement applies; attach IRU declaration for TRC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: monthly penalty of ZAR 250 (or 1% of assessed taxable income if higher) per month, capped at 121 months; non-submission: SARS may issue a directive under s210 Tax Administration Act. Understatement penalty: 10% (substantial non-disclosure) to 200% (intentional evasion). Interest under s89bis at the prescribed rate on unpaid tax. Directors may be held jointly and severally liable for penalties if they caused the non-compliance (s11 TAA).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (dividends tax on any dividend paid by a South African company, payable to SARS by the company as the withholding agent, regardless of whether the dividend is declared from profits; no secondary company tax applies).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident beneficial owner may reduce or eliminate the dividend WHT by completing a dividend tax declaration (DTE) and submitting to the paying company a valid South African Revenue Service (SARS) Tax Residency Certificate (TRC). The declaration must be provided at least 10 days before payment. The paying company retains the declaration and pays 20% only if no DTA relief exists; if a DTA reduces the rate (e.g., 5% under certain treaties) and the shareholder is the residual owner and meets limitation-of-benefits provisions, SARS may refund any excess WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 15% withholding tax, reduced to 0% for interest to certain OECD/treaty lenders or subject to a 5%/10% DTA reduction; Royalties: statutory 15% withholding tax, reduced under DTA (e.g., 0% or 5% depending on treaty). IP licensing of the fitness app to a foreign subsidiary is an 'affected transaction' subject to s31. Non-resident licensor must submit TRC and DQT form to obtain reduced rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: ZAR 1,000,000,000 (R1 billion) – mandatory Master File and Local File for a South African-resident company belonging to an MNE group whose consolidated group revenue exceeds R1 billion; irrespective of threshold, s31 requires contemporaneous, defensible transfer pricing documentation for all 'affected transactions' with non-resident connected persons exceeding ZAR 5 million per annum (domestic transactions apply a ZAR 50 million taxpayer turnover threshold).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa lacks a separate Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the 'place of effective management' (POEM) statutory test requires that a company's senior management and strategic decisions occur in South Africa; the GAAR (s80A–80L) and substance-over-form doctrine allow SARS to disregard a corporate vehicle lacking commercial rationale and substance, particularly a digital royalties pipeline.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deleting or underreporting Google Play / Apple IAP subscription revenue generated by the health fitness app tracker, or invoicing through a non-existent foreign shell to avoid South African tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under s235 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, a criminal fine not exceeding ZAR 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. During trial, the State may also impose a civil understatement penalty between 50% and 200% of the shortfall; SARS may immediately issue an estimated assessment using a 'grossing-up' calculation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly caused or authorised the misstatement may be held personally and jointly liable under s11 TAA for the company's tax debt, restitution to SARS, travel bans under s37C, and imprisonment of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the (Pty) Ltd as a pure conduit without employees, premises, or decision-making power; receiving intercompany royalties for the app IP from a connected Delaware subsidiary without any functional conduct in South Africa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may invoke s80A–80L GAAR to cancel the tax benefit, re-attribute the income to the shareholders, and impose a 75% 'no reasonable care' understatement penalty. The company may lose treaty relief as the 'disregarded entity' is not the beneficial owner for DTA purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil liability for failing to disclose material facts in the ITR14; SARS can apply to the High Court to see through the corporate veil per the Companies Act, enabling attachment of personal assets for unpaid taxes and penalties; repeat offenders may face a travel deregistration and a bar from obtaining the SARS Good Standing certificate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging an excessive arm's-length royalty or service fee to the South African Pty Ltd for use of a fitness app's analytics algorithm, or granting a non-recourse intercompany loan with no demonstrable interest-rate benchmark, thereby shifting profit to a zero-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS conducts an s31 primary adjustment by re-pricing the intercompany transaction at arm's length; the resulting 'dividend in the form of the secondary adjustment' is taxed at 20% dividends tax, plus 100% understatement penalty for 'international tax avoidance' and interest running from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing inferior transfer pricing documentation may be assessed personally for penalty amounts under s204 TAA; in the Companies Act, gross negligence in corporate authorisation constitutes a breach of fiduciary duty, allowing shareholders to recover from the director's personal estate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to appoint a Compliance Officer, perform Know-Your-Customer on digital subscribers, or file a suspicious transaction report (STR) when the app collects debit/credit card data that indicates possible money-laundering; or failing to limit transactions to authorized payment rails (Apple IAP/Google Play) in circumvention of the FIC Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, an accountable institution (any digital payment intermediary or app with payment facilitation) faces an administrative fine up to ZAR 45 million; for non-compliance, criminal liability: fine of up to ZAR 10 million or imprisonment of up to 15 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be disqualified under the Companies Act for an offence under FIC Act; if the FIC issues a directive imposing civil penalty, the director's personal estate is liable unless the director proves compliance; a travel ban directs the Department of Home Affairs to withhold a visa for foreign directors.
